title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
event_hint: Kairos: a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler for disaggregated LLM serving (on vLLM 0.18.1) that reroutes a request's prefill phase to a decode node as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with in-flight decodes, eliminating the inter-node KV transfer for deflected requests; evaluated on the Bursty production-derived trace with DeepSeek-V2-Lite against PD Disaggregation and TaiChi on Azure A100 nodes.
problem: Disaggregated LLM serving (Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, TetriInfer) runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools, but under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate and queue while decode nodes run underutilized (decode is memory-bound and leaves compute slack unused). On a production-style 2P2D A100 cluster, prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 TTFT; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait and inter-node GPU-GPU KV-cache transfer. Static threshold-based deflection policies leave performance on the table.
mechanism: Kairos is a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler (approx. 2000 lines of Python on vLLM 0.18.1, per-request overhead <1 ms via Algorithm 1's deflection-decision loop) that lets a decode node execute a queued request's prefill phase as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with its in-flight decode batch; because the deflected request's prefill runs in place on the decode node, the inter-node KV transfer is eliminated. For each queued request the Dispatcher computes: (1) expected prefill-node TTFT = queue wait + prefill time (Eq. 1); (2) for each decode node, a TBT-safe chunk schedule built by greedily picking the largest safe chunk via LargestSafe (Eq. 5) and summing step latencies (Eq. 6); (3) deflects to the fastest feasible decode node iff its projected TTFT <= alpha * prefill-node TTFT AND <= TTFT_SLO (Eq. 7). TBT safety is enforced by three closed-form analytical step-latency predictors (prefill, decode, mixed batches) plus a transfer-time model, all fit by one-time profiling per model-hardware combination and validated at MAPE < 10% on held-out traces. Single operator knob alpha>=1 (alpha=1 deflects only when strictly faster; alpha>1 allows bounded TTFT regression to relieve the prefill queue within the request's own TTFT SLO). Decode nodes report updated (B_n, K_n) state every heartbeat (Delta_h = 100ms).

evidence.claim: P95 TTFT breakdown on the 2P2D A100 cluster (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, normalized production trace): prefill execution is only 2-23% of end-to-end P95 TTFT across all five workloads; the rest is prefill queue wait + inter-node KV-cache transfer. E.g. Bursty P95 TTFT 7893.9 ms = prefill queue 840.8 + prefill exec 1070.1 + KV transfer 2175.6 + decode queue 55.6 ms; LPLD P95 6278.8 ms with KV transfer alone 4205.4 ms; HPHD KV transfer 3584.6 ms.
evidence.value: prefill exec 2-23% of P95 TTFT; KV transfer up to 4.2s P95 (LPLD), 3.5s (HPHD), 2.1s (Bursty)
evidence.baseline: measured prefill execution share within end-to-end P95 TTFT
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5 (Table 3 P95 TTFT breakdown); PDF Page 4 (Claim 2)

evidence.claim: Complementary utilization (Table 2): across all workloads prefill SM utilization is 75-84% while decode SM utilization never exceeds 27% (LPHD peak 26.4%; HPLD as low as 7.5%); prefill HBM BW use under 1.6% of A100 2TB/s peak and decode under 1%, confirming prefill is compute-bound and decode leaves compute slack.
evidence.value: prefill SM 75-84%; decode SM <=27%; prefill BW <1.6% peak; decode BW <1% peak
evidence.condition: steady-state on 2P2D cluster, mean +/- s.d. over five workloads

evidence.claim: Evaluation setup and baselines (Section 6.1): experiments on Azure ML Standard_ND96amsr_A100_v4 nodes (8x A100-SXM4-80GB per node, NVLink 3.0, AMD EPYC 7V12 64-core, 900 GiB host memory, InfiniBand + Azure Accelerated Networking for inter-node); model DeepSeek-V2-Lite (16B total / 2.4B active MoE) on the Bursty trace; SLO targets P95 TTFT <= 4s and P95 TBT <= 70ms (both must hold simultaneously). Two named baselines: PD Disaggregation (DistServe-style, all prefill on prefill nodes) and TaiChi (unified aggregation/disaggregation with differentiated instances and flowing-decode scheduling).
evidence.value: Azure ND96amsr_A100_v4 (8x A100-SXM4-80GB/node, NVLink 3.0, IB); DeepSeek-V2-Lite 16B/2.4B-active; SLO P95 TTFT<=4s & P95 TBT<=70ms; baselines PD Disaggregation + TaiChi

evidence.claim: Q1 tail-latency result (Figure 4): on the Bursty trace across RPS 6-12, Kairos stays within both P95 TTFT and P95 TBT SLO up to 9 RPS, while PD Disaggregation and TaiChi violate both TTFT and TBT SLO at high request rates (TaiChi violates both); Kairos's deflection decision loop completes in <1 ms per request.
evidence.value: Kairos within SLO up to 9 RPS; baselines violate TTFT/TBT SLO at high RPS; <1 ms per-request decision
evidence.condition: Bursty trace, RPS 6-12, P95 TTFT<=4s & P95 TBT<=70ms
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 9 (Section 6.2 Q1, Figure 4); PDF Page 9 (Algorithm 1 narrative)

evidence.claim: Predictor accuracy and design (Section 5.2): three closed-form analytical step-latency predictors (prefill, decode, mixed) plus a transfer-time model, each requiring only one-time profiling per model-hardware pair; on held-out traces from Table 1 both step-latency predictors achieve MAPE < 10%, sufficient to reliably rank (chunk size, decode node) pairs. Related-systems comparison (Table 5) positions Kairos's per-request TBT-safe chunk-sweep deflection against Sarathi (intra-node token chunking), Nexus (intra-GPU SM partition), PPD (cross-node append-prefill for Turn 2+), TaiChi, Splitwise, DistServe.
evidence.value: step-latency predictors MAPE < 10%; one-time profiling per model-hardware pair
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 6 (Section 5.2 Analytical models); PDF Page 9 (Table 5)

evaluation_context: Production cluster: 2 prefill + 2 decode nodes (2P2D), each NVIDIA A100 80GB (compared against 1P3D and 3P1D on Bursty: 1P3D saturates the single prefill node with median prefill queue >2x 2P2D; 3P1D is decode-capacity-limited with KV-cache-occupancy transfer back-pressure). Evaluation hardware: Azure ML Standard_ND96amsr_A100_v4 nodes, 8x A100-SXM4-80GB per node, NVLink 3.0, AMD EPYC 7V12 64-core, 900 GiB host memory, InfiniBand + Azure Accelerated Networking for inter-node communication. Model: DeepSeek-V2-Lite (16B total / 2.4B active MoE). Evaluated workload: Bursty trace (long-tailed production distribution, Gamma inter-arrivals), the most realistic of the five traces. SLO: P95 TTFT <= 4s AND P95 TBT <= 70ms simultaneously. Baselines: PD Disaggregation (DistServe-style) and TaiChi (unified agg/disagg with flowing-decode scheduling). Dispatcher: per-request Algorithm 1 sweep completes in <1 ms; decode nodes report state every heartbeat Delta_h=100ms. Headline -81% P95 TTFT / +79% SLO attainment are reported as 'up to' maxima over the Bursty trace RPS range.
limitations: The supplement names the baselines (PD Disaggregation = DistServe-style, TaiChi) and hardware and shows Kairos holds SLO up to 9 RPS while baselines violate it, but it does not provide a clean per-RPS table with the exact P95 TTFT (ms) and SLO attainment (%) values behind the headline -81%/+79% maxima; those maxima are read off the Figure 4 curves and the Q2/Q3 results (referenced but the full per-workload improvement table is still beyond the combined visible evidence). Scope: small 2P2D cluster on Azure A100 nodes with DeepSeek-V2-Lite only on the Bursty trace; larger clusters, other models, and non-MoE architectures are not tested. The <1 ms routing overhead is per-request and excludes one-time deployment-time profiling; the centralized dispatcher could become a CPU bottleneck at very high RPS (mitigation: shard by node groups, sacrificing global optimality). Single-deflection-per-heartbeat limit (a decode node accepts one deflected request per 100ms heartbeat); this becomes a bottleneck only at RPS >= |decode nodes| / Delta_h >= 20, above the SLO-supported RPS. Kairos does not account for prefix-cache residency: deflecting a request loses any prefix already cached on the prefill node. KV-transfer elimination applies only to deflected requests; non-deflected requests still incur inter-node KV transfer. RDMA/InfiniBand assumed.
project_relevance: Highly relevant to the TPN card's questions: (1) Kairos is explicitly state-aware — it computes per-request expected TTFT and per-decode-node TBT headroom at scheduling time and deflects based on a TTFT/TBT condition, directly addressing whether the scheduler senses inference phase and KV position; (2) it targets the KV-cache cross-node transfer cost (the dominant 77-98% remainder of P95 TTFT) by eliminating the inter-node KV transfer for deflected requests; (3) it reports end-to-end P95 TTFT and SLO attainment vs named baselines (PD Disaggregation, TaiChi) on the Bursty trace, not just microbenchmarks. It is a concrete answer to what scheduler-side, KV-aware deflection adds over pure GPU-memory scheduling: it exploits decode-side compute slack to remove the transfer that GPU-memory scheduling alone cannot. Caveat: the small 2P2D scale, single Bursty trace, and the 'up to' headline maxima read off Figure 4 still bound the deployable magnitude claim.
